Starting with small electronics in Jakarta. This list is built into the app; it isn\'t a live map or a list of the nearest places, and it doesn\'t need location permission.
Check with the operator before you go. Official sources list these points, but drop box locations, building access, hours, and accepted items can change. Nobody has checked them on site yet.

Accepted items and limits
Small electronics drop box. Check what they accept first.

The Jakarta Environment Agency lists small electronics such as phones, chargers, cables, and power banks. The drop box list mentions a 20 × 5 cm opening, so don\'t force items in. Loose or damaged batteries, light bulbs, chemicals, and large electronics need a specialist route. This point doesn\'t take general plastic, paper, glass, or organic waste.

Wipe your personal data following the manufacturer\'s instructions. Don\'t remove built-in batteries. If a battery is swollen, leaking, hot, or damaged, contact the manufacturer or operator first instead of dropping it in the box.
Hours and access

The source list doesn\'t give the drop box hours or its exact spot in the building. Don\'t assume the building or drop box is open around the clock. Ask building staff or the Jakarta Environment Agency before you bring anything.
Jakarta Environment Agency: (021) 8092744, dinaslh@jakarta.go.id. This contact belongs to the city service, not WasteNot.
